description.short_caption: Large tense bullae on erythematous skin.
description.detailed_description: This clinical photograph shows multiple large, tense bullae on an erythematous base, distributed over the skin of the lower extremity. The bullae appear fluid-filled and intact, with surrounding redness and mild swelling. The skin texture suggests an acute inflammatory process, possibly infectious or autoimmune in origin.

This image shows a Gram stain of an aspirate. Multiple rod-shaped bacteria are visible, stained purple, consistent with gram-positive bacilli. The background is lightly stained, and no other cellular elements are prominently visible. The rods are scattered and vary slightly in size and orientation.
visible_findings: purple staining consistent with gram-positive organisms

description.short_caption: Tissue gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a tissue gram stain with numerous gram-positive bacilli visible as purple rod-shaped structures. The background consists of yellow-stained tissue matrix, likely collagen or extracellular material. The bacilli are scattered throughout the field, with some clustering in certain areas. The staining highlights the bacterial morphology and their distribution within the tissue.
